motivation: Common category pricing and coordinated inventory entry motivate examining product-level performance and a separate common opportunity-cost approximation. Neither is selected because of resulting interval width.
qualification: Category costs mean common opportunity value for device/model storage condition, not equal historical invoice costs. Product-group deviations require the maintained absence of demand spillovers between groups. Group performance prevents unrestricted offsetting of gains and losses across groups; it is stronger than pooled performance.
